transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

This is most likely a blocked defrost drain. Defrost water cannot run away, so it backs up and ends up underneath the salad drawers. 1. Switch the fridge off and unplug it. Remove the salad drawers and dry the area.
2. Look at the bottom of the inside back wall for a small hole or channel. Clear any debris gently with a soft pipe cleaner or cotton bud—do not use anything sharp.
3. Flush it with a small amount of warm water using a squeezy bottle or turkey baster. It should drain away rather than pool back inside. If the hole is frozen solid or the water will not pass through, it may need a full defrost first: leave it off with the doors open, towels down, until all ice has melted, then clear and flush the drain. If it still returns after the drain flows freely, the next suspects are a poor door seal causing excess condensation, or—on a fridge with a water/ice dispenser—a leaking water pipe at the back.

ok thanks, ive unpluged it and took the draws out. theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall with bits of lettuce and gunk in it. il clear it with a cotton bud and warm water, is that right?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
Yes — that is the right approach. With it still unplugged, gently lift out the lettuce/gunk with the cotton bud, then use a small amount of warm (not boiling) water to flush the hole. Do not force anything sharp into it. The debris in the drain points to a blocked defrost drain/drain hose as the cause of the water under the salad drawers. If the water drains away rather than pooling back into the groove, dry the area and monitor it over the next day or two. What make and model is the fridge-freezer? The label is usually inside the fridge, often on a side wall near the salad drawer. If it is not accessible right now, that can wait.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

ive cleared it with the cotton bud and warm water and the water went straight down, so thats good. the sticker says its a Beko CFG1582W, about 4 years old. do i just plug it back in and keep an eye on it?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
Yes — plug it back in, dry the groove and area under the drawers, then keep an eye on it over the next few days. The food debris in the drain and the fact that warm water then ran straight through make a blocked defrost drain the clear cause. To help prevent it returning, keep loose leaves and packaging away from the back-wall groove, and give the drain hole a gentle warm-water flush if you notice any debris collecting there again. If water returns despite the drain still flowing freely, the next things to check would be the door seal and whether the fridge is sitting level, but I’d expect this clean-out to have fixed it.
